items.title: NHL Roundup: Wild strike quick to end Capitals’ winning streak
items.body: WASHINGTON (AP) — Quinn Hughes and Michael McCarron scored in the first 5:27 for Minnesota, and the Wild held on for a 5-1 victory over the Washington Capitals. Justin Sourdif scored the only goal for Washington in the dying seconds of the second period, but the Capitals’ three-game winning streak came to an end during this visit by the Central Division-leading Wild. Maxim Shabanov’s power-play goal with 2:23 left in the third restored a two-goal margin, and Kirill Kaprizov added an empty-netter for his 500th career point and league-leading 15th goal of the season. With 24.9 seconds left and the goalie back in, Danila Yurov scored one more for Minnesota. Washington had scored at least four goals in five of its previous six games, but the Capitals ran into a stingy Minnesota team and goalie Jesper Wallstedt. The Wild permitted two goals or fewer for the fifth time in six games. PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Travis Konecny scored a goal and assisted on another in his first game since missing more than three weeks with an injury as the Philadelphia Flyers beat the Utah Mammoth 6-3. Konecny, who missed 10 games with a lower-body injury, scored his first goal of the season at 1:06 of the second period, banking a shot off Utah goalie Karel Vejmelka to put Philadelphia up 2-1. He later set up Christian Dvorak for a one-timer from the high slot to extend the lead to 4-1. Konecny also set the tone with his physical play, finishing with four hits. Owen Tippett, who missed the last six games with an upper-body injury, also returned to the lineup for Philadelphia. Matvei Michkov scored the Flyers’ first goal, snapping a shot past Vejmelka for his 10th of the season. items.body: Cammi Granato played with Cindy Curley for the United States women's hockey team in 1990, when they won silver at the inaugural IIHF Women's World Championship. Granato also won gold with the U.S. at the 1998 Nagano Olympics, the first to feature women's hockey, and silver at the 2002 Salt Lake City Olympics. Granato was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2010, one of the first women to receive that honor, and was assistant general manager for the Vancouver Canucks from 2022-26. Now senior advisor for amateur scouting for the Canucks, Granato shares her thoughts on Curley, who will be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday, in a special testimonial. I'm thrilled that Cindy Curley is being inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame. She's the player who I always thought deserved to be in. When she played and was dominating her sport, there wasn't a lot of emphasis on women's hockey in the U.S. I learned about her by happenstance. I played hockey with the boys in Chicago until I was 17 and thought it may be the end of the road for me in hockey because the boys were turning into men. My mom was trying to get me into other sports, knowing that there wasn’t much room for me in men's hockey, and because we didn't know there was women's hockey out east. A father on one of the boys' teams that we were playing gave my mom a pamphlet from Providence College where Cindy was playing. It had their scoring statistics, and she was at the top of the list and dominating the score sheet. When I got that pamphlet, Cindy instantly became my first female hockey idol. I wanted to go to Providence College and do the same thing she was doing. The U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame coach and the youth hockey program he founded nearly 50 years ago are back at Southeast Washington D.C.’s Fort Dupont Ice Arena after it closed in spring 2023 for a $39 million renovation. items.summary: The 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 9. This year's class includes Patrice Bergeron, Cindy Curley, Carey Price, Pekka Rinne and Keith Tkachuk in the Players category, and Brian Burke in the Builders category. Here, NHL.com staff writer Tracey Myers profiles Curley.
items.body: Pioneering forward, Providence College legend won silver medal with U.S. three times The 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 9. This year's class includes Patrice Bergeron , Cindy Curley, Carey Price , Pekka Rinne and Keith Tkachuk in the Players category, and Brian Burke in the Builders category. Here, NHL.com staff writer Tracey Myers profiles Curley. For Cindy Curley, hockey has been the gift that keeps on giving. The 62-year-old who grew up in Stow, Massachusetts, just outside of Boston, loves all the things that hockey brought her, not vice versa. "I never thought hockey owed me anything," she said. "I feel like it'll take me the rest of my life to pay back hockey for all the great opportunities and memories. It's a little surreal, honestly." Curley was one of the pioneers of the women's game, a forward who was part of those first world championship teams from the unofficial tournament in 1987 to the IIHF-sanctioned ones in the 1990s. It's why she is being inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in Toronto on Nov. 9. Curley won silver with the United States at the IIHF Women's World Championship in 1990, 1992 and 1994. Prior to that, she had 225 points (110 goals, 115 assists) in four seasons at Providence College, leading the Friars to Eastern College Athletic Conference championships in 1984 and 1985. She was inducted into the United States Hockey Hall of Fame and the Providence College Athletic Hall of Fame in 2013. A self-avowed Boston Bruins fan, Curley said this year she was wondering about former Bruins captain Patrice Bergeron getting into the Hall of Fame more than her own chance at it. items.body: ANAHEIM, Calif. — Cutter Gauthier had his second career hat trick, scoring the go-ahead goal early in the third period, and the Anaheim Ducks overcame a three-goal deficit to beat the Ottawa Senators 6-3 on Sunday night. Judd Caulfield scored twice, rookie Roger McQueen added another and Leo Carlsson had three assists to help the Ducks win for the second time in nine games. Anaheim went 4 for 5 on the power play. Laurent Brossoit made 20 saves in his Anaheim debut. Brossoit played his second NHL game in three seasons after being recalled from San Diego of the AHL on Saturday. Claude Giroux had a goal and an assist as the Senators lost for the third time on a five-game trip. Thomas Chabot and Michael Amadio also scored first-period goals while Jonas Johansson made 27 saves. After the Ducks rallied to tie it at 3 in the second period, they took advantage of a two-man advantage at 1:50 of the third when Gauthier scored from a sharp angle past Johansson. While still on a man advantage, Gauthier scored 36 seconds later for a two-goal cushion.

items.title: McDavid becomes fastest player in NHL history to reach 30 assists in a season
items.body: Connor McDavid 's torrid start to the season just keeps going. The Edmonton Oilers captain made NHL history on Sunday night, becoming the fastest player ever to hit 30 assists in a season. McDavid earned his 30th helper on Evan Bouchard's second-period power-play goal against the New York Rangers on Sunday night, hitting the milestone in just 15 games. Wayne Gretzky held the previous record, earning his 30th assist in his 16th game during the 1984-85 season. McDavid has earned at least one assist in all of the Oilers' games so far this season — a feat that broke an NHL record on Thursday with his 13th consecutive game with an assist. He's now up to 15 consecutive games. It's not just the helpers that are coming for McDavid — he's also been piling on the goals. In 15 games, the three-time Hart Trophy winner has nine goals and 39 points, on pace for 218 points over an 84-game season. The 30-year-old can continue to build on his record when the Oilers take on the Devils on Tuesday.

items.title: Connor McDavid has goal and assist to lead Oilers past Rangers
items.body: NEW YORK — Connor McDavid scored a goal and extended his NHL record season-opening assists streak to 15 games, powering the Edmonton Oilers past the New York Rangers 4-1 on Sunday. On his first shift, McDavid added to his highlight reel and showed why he is widely considered the best hockey player in the world. He banked the puck off the boards to himself, shifted into another gear, blew past defenceman Vladislav Gavrikov and beat Dylan Garand. The goal 50 seconds in broke a tie with two Hall of Famers: the 418th of his career passed Glenn Anderson for the fourth most in franchise history, and his eighth in the first minute of a game put him past Mark Messier for the most with the Oilers. McDavid is the fastest player in league history to 30 assists, leads all scorers with 39 points and is on pace to join Wayne Gretzky as the only players to reach 200 in a season. Evan Bouchard had a goal and two assists to join Bobby Orr, Al MacInnis and Denis Potvin as the only defencemen with 25-plus points in his first 15 games. Journeyman goaltender Matt Tomkins, making his first start for Edmonton and seventh in the NHL, backstopped the team to its third consecutive victory by making some key saves among his 28. Colton Dach had two goals, including an empty-netter with 39.4 seconds left to seal it. The Oilers are 7-0 on the road. Garand, allowed three goals on 24 shots in his ninth consecutive appearance since Igor Shesterkin went down with a right knee injury. Pavel Dorofeyev scored for the Rangers, who have lost four in a row and six of their past seven after a strong start.

items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Travis Konecny scored a goal and assisted on another in his first game since missing more than three weeks with an injury as the Philadelphia Flyers beat the Utah Mammoth 6-3 on Sunday. Konecny, who missed 10 games with a lower-body injury, scored his first goal of the season at 1:06 of the second period, banking a shot off Utah goalie Karel Vejmelka to put Philadelphia up 2-1. He later set up Christian Dvorak for a one-timer from the high slot to extend the lead to 4-1. Konecny also set the tone with his physical play, finishing with four hits. Owen Tippett, who missed the last six games with an upper body injury, also returned to the lineup for Philadelphia. Matvei Michkov scored the Flyers' first goal, snapping a shot past Vejmelka for his 10th of the season. He became the first Flyer to score 10 goals in his first 17 games of a season since Konecny did it in 2023. Dvorak and Noah Cates also finished with a goal and an assist each. Oliver Bonk added a goal for Philadelphia and Dan Vladar made 19 saves as the Flyers snapped a three-game winless streak (0-2-1). Dmitri Simashev scored Utah's first goal, Mikhail Sergachev added a late power-play goal for Utah, and Logan Cooley scored his eighth goal this season with the extra attacker on the ice, before Cole Knuble iced the game for Philadelphia with an empty-net goal. Vejmelka made 15 saves as the Mammoth have alternated wins and losses over their past eight games. Mammoth: Continue their six-game road trip in Toronto on Tuesday night.

Cole Hutson found him on the doorstep with a pass early in the third period, but with the net open, the puck bounced off Ovechkin's skate and he wasn't able to control it. items.body: Center has four points in 14 games this season; Seattle receives Wood in return Shane Wright was traded to the Nashville Predators by the Seattle Kraken for Matthew Wood on Sunday. Wright, the No. 4 pick in the 2022 NHL Draft, has four points (three goals, one assist) in 14 games this season. The center played 167 games with the Kraken since the start of 2024-25 after playing the majority of the previous season with Coachella Valley of the American Hockey League. The 22-year-old has 82 points (39 goals, 43 assists) in 183 NHL games. Wright had nine points (two goals, seven assists) in 24 AHL playoff games in 2023, helping Coachella Valley reach the Calder Cup Finals before losing to Hershey. “We are excited to add Shane to our mix of forwards,” Nashville general manager Chris MacFarland said. “We feel he will bring a strong, two-way game to our team and will add to the pace of our lineup. We believe Shane will continue to grow as a player, and we look forward to working with him.” The Predators (5-4-5) host the Carolina Hurricanes on Tuesday (8 p.m. ET; HHN, CARNHL, SCRIPPS, SN+). Wood had three points (one goal, two assists) in 14 games for the Predators this season. The 21-year-old forward was a first-round pick (No. 15) by Nashville at the 2023 NHL Draft and has 34 points (18 goals, 16 assists) in 91 games. “There's still room to add more strength to his body and to his frame,” Kraken general manager Jason Botterill said. “But I think he utilizes his reach very well to protect pucks. And more importantly, to get a shot off. And we think his hockey sense and his shot are two of the best attributes that he can bring to our team.” The Kraken (8-5-1) host the Calgary Flames on Wednesday (10 p.m. ET; Prime Video, KONG, SNW).

items.summary: The Predators and Kraken swap former first-round picks as Wright finally finds a change of scenery.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Nashville Predators and Seattle Kraken will be swapping a couple of young talents, with center Shane Wright going to Nashville and winger Matthew Wood going to Seattle. The trade comes after Wright finding himself in trade rumours for a significant amount of time, as he has yet to live up to the pedigree of a fourth-overall pick with the Kraken. The Predators swing a deal looking to take a gamble on him in hopes that they finally can find a long-term solution to their center depth. Wright has started the season on a slower note, as he has just three goals and one assist for four points in 14 games before the trade. He’s shown flashes of being the player he was originally drafted to be, but up to this point, he hasn’t had a more successful season than his 19-goal, 44-point campaign in 2024-25. Wright is in the final year of his three-year entry-level contract with an $886,666 cap hit, a contract which has lasted five years due to the contract sliding for the first two seasons. He’ll be a restricted free agent at the end of the season. In return for Wright, the Kraken acquire Wood, who has become one of the more intriguing young power forwards in the league. He caught the hockey world’s attention not just with his six-foot-four, 202-pound frame, but also with his rookie campaign, which saw him get 17 goals and 13 assists for 30 points in 71 games. But like Wright, Wood has also had a slower start to the season, with just one goal and two assists for three points in 14 games. If there’s any concern for the Kraken with this trade, it’s that Wood doesn’t end up like the last goal-scoring power forward from the Preds’ system: Tanner Jeannot broke out with a 24-goal rookie season, but has since only scored 27 goals in the five seasons following it.

items.body: RALEIGH, N.C. — Pyotr Kochetkov ’s 26-save shutout gave him 10 straight victories to begin the season, Sean Walker scored two goals, and the Carolina Hurricanes beat the Winnipeg Jets 7-0 on Sunday. Kochetkov became the third goalie in NHL history to start a season at 10-0. Sebastian Aho, Juuso Valimaki, Logan Stankoven, Mark Jankowski and Jesperi Kotkaniemi also scored for the Hurricanes, who’ve won four in a row. Stankoven, Seth Jarvis, Nikolaj Ehlers and Shayne Gostisbehere all had two assists. Kochetkov tied Carey Price’s 10-win mark with Montreal from 10 years ago for the second-longest season-opening streak. Only Jack Campbell holds a longer season-beginning mark with 11 consecutive victories for the Toronto Maple Leafs in 2020-21. Kochetkov’s second shutout of the season pushed his career total to 13 in 135 games. The Jets have lost nine games in a row (0-7-2). Stuart Skinner, who made 12 saves, was pulled after allowing the fifth goal. Clay Stevenson stopped 13 shots in relief. Walker’s short-handed goal began the scoring 5:16 into the game. Aho’s power-play tally came during Carolina’s four-goal spree in the first 10 minutes of the second period. Stankoven’s goal at 9:09 of the second period stretched the lead to 5-0. At the time, the Jets had five total shots on goal. It’s Walker’s his first two-goal output in two seasons with the Hurricanes. Jets: Tuesday night at Montreal to end a four-game road trip.

items.body: Register Login Capitals Place Dylan McIlrath On Waivers By Brennan McClain | at November 1, 2026 1:45 pm The Washington Capitals needed to clear a roster spot after acquiring netminder Rémi Poirier from the New Jersey Devils earlier this morning. To that end, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman said the Capitals placed defenseman Dylan McIlrath on waivers. According to beat reporter Sammi Silber, Washington is planning to keep three netminders on the roster for the foreseeable future. The Capitals recently ran into some injury troubles with starter Logan Thompson , so Poirier will give them some insurance behind Charlie Lindgren . Regardless, the acquisition of Poirier will cost McIlrath his roster spot. The former 10th overall pick of the 2010 NHL Draft is in his sixth season with the Capitals after signing as an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2021-22 season. Despite the relatively lengthy tenure with the Capitals organization, it hasn’t come with a lot of ice time. Since the beginning of the 2022-23 season, McIlrath has skated in 43 games for Washington, tallying four assists while averaging 10:34 of ice time per game. McIlrath has also delivered 90 hits during that stretch. Although he hasn’t registered many games with the Capitals, he’s remained on the roster as a seventh or eighth defenseman. If he clears waivers, McIlrath will return to a familiar environment in the AHL. He played in 192 games for the Hershey Bears during his first three years with the Capitals organization, scoring seven goals and 32 points. Not only did McIlrath help the Bears win back-to-back Calder Cup championships in 2023 and 2024, but he was also the team’s captain.

Poirier, 25, was drafted 185th overall by the Dallas Stars in the 2020 NHL Draft. The Farnham, QC, native was playing with the QMJHL’s Gatineau Olympiques at the time, earning a career record of 62-46-13 with a .902 SV% and 3.06 GAA. The former sixth-round pick joined the professional ranks in the 2023-24 campaign, splitting his time between the AHL’s Texas Stars and the ECHL’s Idaho Steelheads. Surprisingly, the Devils claimed Poirier off waivers from the Stars ahead of the 2026-27 season. New Jersey already had Jake Allen and Nico Daws rostered, so the addition of Poirier raised some questions. Despite spending an entire month with the Devils, he never appeared in a game for them and was rarely invited to practice. items.body: Nikita Zadorov 's wallet has taken a hit after sucker-punching Alex Vlasic . items.title: Sunday Overreactions: Lightning, Wild can’t risk losing stars for nothing
items.summary: The Lightning and Wild find themselves in similar positions, needing to decide the best course of action with stars Nikita Kucherov and Quinn Hughes on expiring contracts. Michael Amato explores their conundrum and more in his Sunday Overreactions.
items.body: Last Friday, Connor Hellebuyck was on the move. A little over a year ago, Quinn Hughes was dealt on a Friday. So were Mikko Rantanen and Matthew Tkachuk before him. Now we’ve learned this past Friday that Nikita Kucherov doesn’t intend to re-sign with the Tampa Bay Lightning , and he has requested a trade. That news was nothing short of colossal, and it has the potential to completely reshape the balance of the Atlantic Division and the Eastern Conference. A Kucherov extension was always going to be complicated . He’s an elite player coming off a Hart Trophy in a market that has exploded, but Kucherov is also going to be 34 when this new deal kicks in, and the Lightning are known for trying to get a bargain in contract negotiations. They still don’t have a $10-million player and a Kucherov extension would blow their internal cap out of the water. However, that’s the reality of today’s NHL. There’s no putting the toothpaste back in the tube. If the Lightning won’t give Kucherov what he wants, someone else will next summer, regardless of his age. Now Julien BriseBois finds himself in a similar position to Bill Guerin, having a player unsigned beyond this season who is a critical piece of a Stanley Cup push. Keeping Kucherov and Quinn Hughes in the fold would no doubt help the Lightning and the Minnesota Wild achieve their goals, but you also run the major risk of losing them for nothing. Wild and Lightning should trade Hughes and Kucherov if they don’t extend BriseBois was emphatic in a statement following the Kucherov news that he has no plans to trade his superstar. Fowler edged Boston Bruins center James Hagens (5-6—11 in 14 GP), Toronto Maple Leafs left wing Gavin McKenna (5-6—11 in 14 GP), San Jose Sharks left wing Ivar Stenberg (3-6—9 in 15 GP) and New York Rangers goaltender Dylan Garand (4-5-1, 2.69 GAA, .899 SV%, 1 SO) for the honor. The last rookie on any team to post a longer winning streak was Boston’s Jeremy Swayman from Feb. 19 – March 12, 2022 (8-0-0). Martin Necas and Brock Nelson also scored, and defenceman Cale Makar had four assists for the Avalanche. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves. Colorado has won two in a row against opponents playing on the second night of a back-to-back. The Avalanche defeated New Jersey on Wednesday and faced Calgary’s No. 3 goaltender, Arsenii Sergeev , less than 24 hours after the Flames beat Seattle. Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil scored for Calgary. Sergeev made 29 saves in his second career start and first this season. Sergeev was recalled from the AHL when the Flames placed Devin Cooley on the injured list with a lower-body injury. Colorado was not whistled for a penalty, while Calgary took three — two on a double-minor late in the third period. The Avalanche, who lost defenceman Josh Manson for two months after he injured an ankle against the Devils, saw Nelson exit in the second when he took a shot by Makar off the side of his helmet. Nelson, who scored earlier in the period, was able to skate to the bench and down the tunnel. He returned in the third period. Nelson capped a three-goal burst in the first 10 minutes of the second that gave Colorado a 4-0 lead. Farabee scored 1:43 after Nelson’s goal, and Pospisil made it 4-2 when he scored 1:59 into the third. Lehkonen deflected Makar’s shot from the point at 4:09 to make it 5-2. items.title: Canucks starting to deliver on effort, competitiveness despite loss
items.summary: Nobody promised wins. But the Vancouver Canucks are finally starting to deliver on the effort and competitiveness they pledged as a baseline.
items.body: VANCOUVER – Nobody promised wins. But the Vancouver Canucks are finally starting to deliver on the effort and competitiveness they pledged as a baseline. Their 4-2 loss Saturday to the Toronto Maple Leafs dropped the Canucks to 3-12-1, which is grotesque and worse than anyone expected even for the start of a National Hockey League rebuild. But they had their goalie out and pressing for a late tying goal, as they did in Thursday’s 3-2 road loss to the San Jose Sharks, and the Canucks didn’t drown at five-on-five against another superstar-driven team. And even though Vancouver’s poor middle period decided the game, the two shots that allowed Toronto to go ahead 3-1 could have been handled better by goalie Leevi Merilainen. After getting outshot in 12 of their first 13 games, which included a 10-game losing streak, the Canucks have now narrowly outshot their opponents in three straight contests. Shots on Saturday were 29-28. It is sobering that these last three games, a 6-5 overtime win against the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday followed by the goalie-out losses against the Sharks and Leafs, probably constitute a “hot streak” at this stage for the NHL’s worst team. But at least there is progress, which was difficult to find through most of October – a month that was Halloween for the Canucks from start to finish. “Getting closer,” coach Manny Malhotra said Saturday night. “It's not close to where we need to be or need to get to, but there is progress there. It's frustrating as we talk about these games after loss after loss, but we do see improvement in different areas of our game. It's just... tough to see those when there's no correlation to wins.” “Obviously, the end result has to change somehow,” Canucks winger Paul Cotter , part of an effective fourth line, told Sportsnet.

items.title: Kucherov would consider trade to Maple Leafs or Canadiens
items.body: The reigning MVP could have his eyes on the Atlantic Division. The Toronto Maple Leafs and Montreal Canadiens are two teams that Nikita Kucherov would consider as trade destinations, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported during Saturday Night Hockey . Kucherov has a modified no-trade clause, meaning he can submit a list of 10 approved teams he can be traded to. The Russian forward has a 10-team list, but the teams on it are currently unknown, Friedman added. This latest development comes after Kucherov informed both his teammates and the Lightning organization that he will not be re-signing with Tampa Bay and would like to be traded. There was a meeting between Kucherov, his agent Dan Milstein, head coach Jon Cooper, and GM Julien Brisebois on Friday, but they were unable to settle the situation, Friedman reported. The Lightning released a statement saying they would not be trading Kucherov. "We are aware of the media reports regarding the future of Nikita Kucherov with the Lightning," Brisebois said in a statement. "We unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita." Kucherov, 33, is in the final season of an eight-year, $76-million contract and had 130 points (44 goals, 86 assists) last season in his second Hart Trophy-winning campaign. Friedman's reporting also included that Kucherov initially wanted his contract to be in the same territory as Kirill Kaprizov's deal, but that changed after Leo Carlsson's off-season offer sheet. However, the biggest catalyst in Kucherov's decision was the lack of pace in the negotiations.

items.title: Red Wings’ Dylan Larkin may alter trade list
items.body: Another chapter could be coming to the Dylan Larkin saga in Detroit. After making the decision on Thursday to sit out until the Red Wings fulfill his trade request, Larkin might adjust the list of teams that he is willing to waive his no-movement clause for. "He has a 10-team trade list that he's willing to go to," Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman said on the latest Saturday Headlines segment. "I think over the next 24-to-48 hours, it's possible we see that trade list altered." Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press reported on Oct. 20 that Larkin's trade list includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. When Larkin initially requested a trade out of the Motor City, it was reported that he was only open to a move to the Panthers, Wild and Golden Knights. But now that Larkin has opted out of playing with the Red Wings after scoring two goals and six points over 10 games, the club's former captain appears ready to find a spot outside some of the premier American NHL destinations. "Some teams like Florida and Vegas, even Colorado, it's very hard to see (a trade) happening, if not impossible," Friedman said Saturday. "So, I do think it's possible that Larkin may take some teams off, or possibly even add some teams on." Larkin was suspended without pay and taken off the roster by Detroit after the 30-year-old centre informed the team he would no longer play for the franchise. Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said Thursday his goal is to acquire players that can help right away, adding he's open to deals for prospects and draft picks that give the franchise a fair return for someone of Larkin's calibre.

items.summary: Sidney Crosby added another honor to his historic career on Saturday night against the Montreal Canadiens.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Sidney Crosby continues to rack up NHL records and milestones. On Saturday, the Pittsburgh Penguins forward surpassed Ray Bourque for the most assists with a single NHL franchise, with a pair of assists in the first two periods against the Montreal Canadiens. The two assists, first on the opening goal to Erik Karlsson, and later on the 2-2 goal to Tommy Novak, brought him to a total of 1,112, passing Bourque’s 1,111. Wayne Gretzky, despite holding the record for the most assists in NHL history with 1,963, posted only 1,086 of those with the Edmonton Oilers , the team he spent the longest with. Rounding out the top five on the all-time assists-with-one-team leaderboard are Steve Yzerman, with 1,063 assists for the Detroit Red Wings , and Mario Lemieux, with 1,033 assists with the Penguins. Crosby’s first Saturday assist came as the primary to Karlsson’s goal, with Novak providing the secondary assist, bringing him to 100 career NHL assists. Meanwhile, Crosby now has 657 goals and 1,112 assists for 1,769 points in 1,433 regular-season games. In addition, Crosby has netted 72 goals and 134 assists for 206 points in 186 Stanley Cup Playoff games. The latest accolade comes in what has already been a history-making season for Crosby. Lining up alongside Kris Letang and Evgeni Malkin, the trio became the longest group of three to play on a single team , hitting 21 consecutive seasons, and amassed the most wins by a trio together, with 494 on Sept. 30. While Crosby’s point total has been slow to come by at 39 years old, with three goals and four assists for seven points in 13 games heading into the matchup with the Canadiens, he will be hoping for an uptick in production as the Penguins continue through the fall. Even with Los Angeles gaining momentum in the second half of the second period, the Sabres made it 2-0 on Thompson’s ninth with 4:22 left. Perry got the Kings on the board on a power play with 2:36 to go, though they needed a coach’s challenge to overturn a goaltender interference call. Lee tied it 1:29 into the third. items.body: ELMONT, N.Y. — On Halloween day, the Edmonton Oilers came dressed as the 1995 New Jersey Devils. The Oilers simply smothered a tired New York Islanders team Saturday on Long Island, constricting New York in a 4-0 win — their second straight one as Edmonton strings together six consecutive periods of perfect defensive hockey. At 10-2-2 thus far in the 2026-27 season, Edmonton continues to win games with their defensive play, a trait that has been mostly foreign to the McDavid era in Edmonton. “That was a good team to test that against because they throw everything to the slot,” said defenceman Ryan Shea, who quietly played 22:35 Saturday. “They had nine shots (on goal) through the first two periods and we were doing our jobs. That's what we’ve got to be day in, day out. Speaking of a good spot, how’s the view from the goal crease? Surely, it’s seldom been better, considering the last time Edmonton recorded back-to-back shutouts was Mike Smith in April of 2022, and before that Cam Talbot way back in 2017. “Guys are just committed,” said Tristan Jarry , who faced 24 shots in that 4-0 win over Calgary and just 18 more against the Isles. “They've really bought in from the start of training camp. Obviously, there's a learning curve to a new system and what we're doing. But every day the guys have been working at it, whether it's practice or video. October 24th: With the Blues only carrying a minimum-sized roster at the moment, adding reinforcements at some point was a given. They’ve added one on the back end as they’ve recalled blueliner Quinton Burns from AHL Springfield, per the NHL’s media site. It’s the first career NHL recall for the 21-year-old. Burns was a third-round pick back in 2023 out of OHL Kingston, spending two more seasons with the Frontenacs after being selected. In 2024-25, he had a big season there, tallying 49 points and 100 penalty minutes in 66 contests. That production didn’t carry over to his first professional campaign last season. Burns split the year between the Thunderbirds and ECHL Florida. With the former, he had five assists and 92 penalty minutes in 31 games while with the latter, he collected six points and 17 penalty minutes in 16 appearances. This season, Burns has an assist and 29 penalty minutes through seven outings in Springfield. At first glance, it seems unlikely that Burns will see much action. Theo Lindstein , one of their top defensive prospects, could be back up before long after getting some game action in with the Thunderbirds; he made his season debut with them last night. For now, at least, Burns will get a chance to make an impression on the coaching staff in the hopes of making his NHL debut.

items.title: Matt Pavelich, first linesman in Hockey Hall of Fame, dead at 92
items.body: NEW YORK — Matt Pavelich, the first linesman inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame, has died. He was 92. Pavelich officiated games in 19 consecutive Stanley Cup Finals from 1961-79 as part of his 23 seasons working in the NHL. He took part in 1,727 regular season and 245 playoff games during that stretch before serving as the league's supervisor of officials and going into the Hall in 1987. Commissioner Gary Bettman called Pavelich a true icon of the profession. “No linesman in the history of the National Hockey League was more universally respected nor more widely admired than Matt Pavelich,” Bettman said in a statement. “Pavelich personified professionalism and integrity while possessing a warm personal touch that enabled him to develop working relationships with players and coaches.”

items.title: Opinion: Unlike Hellebuyck And Larkin, Nikita Kucherov Is Doing The Lightning A Solid
items.summary: Nikita Kucherov shocked the NHL by requesting a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning, but unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, he is doing his team a solid by doing so.
items.body: James Guillory-Imagn Images James Guillory-Imagn Images Opinion: Unlike Hellebuyck And Larkin, Nikita Kucherov Is Doing The Lightning A Solid Ken Campbell Partner Oct 31, 2026 4:54 PM Published Oct 31, 2026 4:54 PM Nikita Kucherov shocked the NHL by requesting a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning, but unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, he is doing his team a solid by doing so. Wow, this one is seismic. Among the superstars in the NHL who are asking/demanding they be moved, there's probably not a person in hockey who had Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov on their bingo card. With 13-plus seasons, two Hart Trophies, two Art Ross Trophies, two Stanley Cups, and more than 1,100 career points as the franchise’s leading scorer, Kucherov looked like as sure a bet as you could find to finish his career with the team that drafted him. More Videos But, unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, Kucherov is actually doing his team a favor with his public declaration. For so many reasons, this is different than the other two. And when the dust settles and emotions subside, the Lightning are going to be happy Kucherov greased his own skids out of town.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images The red, white and blue looks clean, calm and cool heading into one of hockey’s biggest events. On Saturday, USA Hockey revealed the 25-player roster set to represent the United States at the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship. Team USA is trotting out 20 of the 23 players who were part of the gold-medal-winning squad at the 2026 Winter Olympics , the team’s first gold at the Winter Games since 2018. The only players who aren’t back on the roster from Milan are Kendall Coyne Schofield, Britta Curl-Salemme and goaltender Ava McNaughton. Coyne Schofield isn’t playing at all this season, as she announced that she’s pregnant with her second child. With so much familiarity throughout the roster, it’s hard not to think the U.S. isn’t on a path to a second consecutive Women’s Worlds gold. Along with Captain America Hilary Knight coming into her record 16th WWC appearance, the U.S. has extensive winning pedigree. Veterans such as Alex Carpenter, Megan Keller and Jesse Compher are all looking to add another medal to their trophy case, while youngsters such as Laila Edwards, Abbey Murphy and Olympic MVP Caroline Harvey look to further solidify themselves as superstars. Goaltending seems to have little holes as well. Aerin Frankel and Gwyneth Philips backstopped the team to the gold at the 2025 WWC and Olympics this past February, with the duo making history in Milan. The one notable difference is the lack of college players. With the Worlds being moved to November, it was expected that some players might not elect to leave campus for the event. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Some reinforcements are coming to the Lone Star State, including an anticipated debut. When speaking to the media at morning skate, Dallas Stars head coach Glen Gulutzan announced that forward David Perron will make his debut on Saturday night, when the Stars take on the Columbus Blue Jackets . He also mentioned that he’s “90 percent” sure that defenseman Esa Lindell will return to the lineup. Perron signed a one-year contract with the Stars on Oct. 16 and has spent the past couple of weeks getting in shape. His deal has a prorated cap hit of $850,000. Perron moves to Dallas hoping to produce a little bit more and stay healthier than he has in the past couple of seasons. After an impressive stretch in which he posted at least 45 points in eight consecutive seasons, the Stanley Cup champion posted only 16 points in 43 games with the Ottawa Senators in 2024-25, improving only slightly to 28 points in 65 appearances last year. He started last season with the Sens before the trade deadline , when he was traded to the Detroit Red Wings , though he did little to improve the team’s postseason chances, scoring just three goals in 16 contests. In 1,239 regular-season games in the NHL, Perron has posted 332 goals and 480 assists for 812 points, with another 64 points in 110 postseason contests. Lindell has missed the past five games due to a lower-body injury. Gulutzan mentioned, at the time, that the veteran blueliner suffered the injury when he blocked a shot in a previous game. items.title: Quick Shifts: How Nikita Kucherov’s trade request helps Lightning
items.summary: There have been some wild reactions to the even wilder bombshell that was Nikita Kucherov’s trade request. But, as Sportsnet’s Luke Fox writes in the latest Quick Shifts, the reigning MVP may actually be doing the Lightning a favour.
items.body: A quick mix of the things we gleaned from the week of hockey, serious and less so, and rolling four lines deep. Same as last week’s column, only spookier. 1. In the wake of Friday afternoon’s Friedge bomb that Nikita Kucherov will not be re-signing with the Tampa Bay Lightning and would like to be moved, we saw some wild reaction to some wilder news. Some compared the Bolts’ newly minted all-time leading scorer’s trade request to that of Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin . No way. Both the Devils goalie and suspended and stripped Red Wings captain have nearly five full years on their current contracts. Both decided to stop honouring those contracts. Kucherov is an impending unrestricted free agent, plans to keep piling points (15 through 12 games) for the team that drafted him in 2011, and is actually doing the franchise he helped to 12 post-seasons and two Stanley Cups a favour. We sat in the arena when walk-for-nothing franchise cornerstones John Tavares and Mitch Marner (Nicolas Roy acknowledged) returned to the homes of their former teams after choosing a fresh path on the open market. At least there is honesty and transparency with Kucherov — and, for that matter, GM Julien BriseBois — as the mini dynasty and its mind-blowing playmaker head for divorce. Until we’re told otherwise, this appears like a matter of money. BriseBois separates sentiment from business. It’s why he refused to pay Tampa’s last all-time legend market value and let Steven Stamkos walk to Nashville. Kucherov will be 34 when he begins his next contract. And with salaries spiking, his next AAV should begin with a 2 and feature eight figures. items.summary: Have any of the seven clubs changed our minds for better or worse so far?

Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images The 2026-27 NHL season remains young, but it has been a competitive one for most of Canada’s teams so far. With the exception of the lowly Vancouver Canucks, every other Canadian club either holds down a playoff position or is within five points of one (with games in hand) through Thursday’s action. So let’s revisit the annual question: Which Canadian teams make the playoffs this season? MATT LARKIN: I’ll say the Edmonton Oilers, Montreal Canadiens and Ottawa Senators . In other words, my pre-season picks are unchanged. The Toronto Maple Leafs have been solid in bursts so far, but their defense is still way too messy for that playoff spot to hold up, I reckon. The Winnipeg Jets’ return in the trade for Connor Hellebuyck won’t bring enough immediate help to get them into the playoffs, and while I appreciate the Calgary Flames’ recent hot streak, it was largely thanks to a surge from goaltender Devin Cooley, who has since landed on injured reserve. PAUL PIDUTTI: Ahead of the season, I had the same three Canadian teams as Matt making the postseason. I’m going to add a fourth: Edmonton, Montreal, Ottawa… and the Winnipeg Jets . items.body: Register Login Avalanche Recall Gavin Brindley By Ryan Long | at October 31, 2026 7:45 am The Colorado Avalanche have recalled forward Gavin Brindley from their AHL affiliate, the Colorado Eagles, the team announced . The move comes just over a week after Brindley was reassigned to the Eagles on October 22. The recall appears to be driven primarily by uncertainty around Logan O’Connor ’s availability for Saturday’s game against the Calgary Flames. O’Connor was not at practice Friday morning ahead of the funeral for his father, Myles, which was held Friday evening, per Corey Masisak of The Denver Post. O’Connor was nearing his season debut from a lower-body injury at the time and stepped away from the team to be with his family. He was activated off long-term injured reserve ahead of Colorado’s October 23 game against the Tampa Bay Lightning and has appeared in each of the club’s last three games, averaging 13:24 of ice time without recording a point. Still, Brindley has made a case for another NHL look. He has four points (one goal, three assists) in four games since his reassignment and finished October as the Eagles’ leading scorer and second star of the month with nine points (two goals, seven assists) in eight games, despite missing two games while with the Avalanche. During his first recall of the season, which began October 14, he recorded one assist in four NHL games while averaging 8:08 of ice time with no special-teams usage. The 22-year-old was acquired from the Columbus Blue Jackets in June 2025, along with a 2025 third-round pick and a conditional 2027 second-round pick, in exchange for Charlie Coyle and Miles Wood .
